_doc: U113 (E5-8; closes G6) / F11 — Unified browser->API->MCP fallback ladder
('inability to fail'), selected PER OPERATION and PER CONNECTED LOCATION.
ONE auditable declaration of the attempt order across the three transports for
each Skill 6 build surface, so the order is testable and never silently drifts
from the code paths it describes. Read by tools/ghl_fallback_ladder.py.
ENABLEMENT IS EXPLICIT (F11): GHL_FALLBACK_LADDER unset => the FULL ladder runs
(failover is the production default; a silently single-rung ladder was the
defect). '1'/'true'/'yes'/'on' => explicit-on. '0'/'false'/'no'/'off' =>
explicit-off: only the first OPERATION rung is attempted — the deliberate
single-rung revert. Any other value is a config error, never a guess. The
chosen state is stamped on every receipt as 'enablement'.
COMPLETION CONTRACT (F11): a rung succeeds only when ok IS the boolean true,
operation_complete IS the boolean true, and 'operation' names the SAME operation
the caller requested — at the connected location. 'prerequisite_ready' and
'partial' are recorded as their own states and are distinct from
'operation_complete'; they never end the ladder.
RUNG KINDS: 'rungs' marks a rung whose success is a PREREQUISITE only. A
prerequisite rung can never report an entire page/form operation complete, even
if it wrongly claims operation_complete — the runner records the contradiction
and keeps walking. Every surface keeps at least one 'operation' rung.
LOCATION: 'location.required' + 'location.carrier' name how the connected
location is bound. A location-required surface is never complete with no bound
location, and a rung's observed location must match the gated tenant.
DOM: 'dom_refresh: true' means a browser rung reached as a FALLBACK (after
another rung has run) must re-establish the page/context and refresh DOM
references through an enter hook (returning 'dom_epoch'). A fallback never
assumes it shares a session with the rung that failed. The PRIMARY browser
rung establishes the session itself and needs no enter hook.
OPERATION NAMING: a surface that declares several operations requires the
caller to name ONE. A rung may not report completion without naming that
same operation; an unnamed completion is recorded as 'partial'.
Every 'order' entry is grounded in a real file this repo already ships — see the
'evidence' map per surface. A surface with only ONE real transport today (no
fabricated second rung) is listed under 'not_laddered' with the reason, never
given an invented fallback (D8 'zero invented selectors' doctrine, generalized).
RETIRED TRANSPORT: the self-hosted community GHL MCP is retired (GU-009/GU-010).
It is not a rung anywhere in this file; the official GHL MCP (Tier 1) is the
only MCP transport.

browser.why: the page builder performs design/insertion the blob cannot express (funnels.pages.authoring)

mcp.why: uploads media objects the page may later reference; an uploaded asset is not a finished page

evidence.api: tools/ghl_survey_rest.py — CANVAS-FREE capture-gated REST fallback (build_method='rest'); refuses to blind-POST, derives the save route ONLY from a recorded capture receipt.

pipeline.reason: single-lane today: GHL exposes NO public API to create a pipeline or pipeline stage (operator-ratified 2026-07-07, confirmed against GHL's real v2 AND v3 OpenAPI specs; only GET /opportunities/pipelines is public). Browser is the ONLY transport. Declaring a second/third rung here would be a fabricated fallback (forbidden). Add a real ladder entry the day GHL ships a create API for this object.
